Use the current working directory for all files.
Create the file case_120.inp in the working directory using exactly the Input deck text provided in the user message.
Write the raw input deck text to case_120.inp without the surrounding ```inp code fences.
Do not include the Reference text section in case_120.inp.
Do not add, delete, or modify any nodes, elements, materials, sections, boundaries, transforms, steps, or other cards in the input deck.
Run CalculiX by first executing `ccx -i case_120`.
If `ccx -i case_120` does not work on the system, run `ccx case_120` instead.
Wait for the CalculiX process to finish before checking the results.
Determine whether the run succeeded by inspecting case_120.sta.
Treat the run as successful only if case_120.sta contains a successful termination message such as 'JOB COMPLETED'.
If case_120.sta is missing or reports failure, treat the run as an error.
Write results.json in the working directory with the keys solver, case_id, status, ccx_version, artifacts, and notes.
Set solver to "calculix".
Set case_id to "case_120".
Set status to "success" if the run terminated successfully according to case_120.sta, otherwise set status to "error".
Set ccx_version to the version string output by `ccx -v`, or the closest equivalent version command on the system.
Set artifacts to an empty array.
In notes, record the exact ccx command that was used.
If the run failed, also record in notes the error message and the file that indicated the failure, such as case_120.sta.
Even if CalculiX does not start or the input deck is rejected, still write results.json with status set to "error".
